name: Labor Zionism
summary: Labor Zionism is the socialist strand of Zionism, holding that a Jewish state in the Land of Israel would be built by a Jewish working class through settlement, cooperative farming and union-run enterprise. Its thinkers differed (Borochov was Marxist, Gordon a mystic of labor, Ben-Gurion a pragmatic statist), but all treated labor and national revival as one project. After 1948 it governed Israel through Mapai and later moved toward land for peace and social democracy.
scope: The mainstream of Labor Zionism from Borochov's Poale Zion (1905-06) and Gordon's Hapoel Hatzair through Ben-Gurion's Mapai and the Histadrut, focused on the 1920s-1960s peak. It excludes Revisionism and religious Zionism, and treats the modern Israeli Labor Party as a later descendant. Social and cultural questions are mostly inferred, so many answers are low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Labor Zionism built the Histadrut with its own sick fund and Mapai belonged to the Socialist International, so state-guaranteed care fits; healthcare itself is not documented in these sources.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A movement built on a Jewish working class and its trade-union federation would favour better pay, though wage floors are inferred rather than documented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Labor Zionists sought a Jewish economy planned and led by the working class through the Histadrut, not left to private markets, though Mapai's socialism was pragmatic.

public-ownership.rationale: The Histadrut ran industry and construction as labor-owned enterprises and Ben-Gurion wanted a Jewish economy under working-class leadership, though Mapai's socialism was pragmatic, so support is moderate.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Socialist and social-democratic orientation implies redistribution, but taxation is not discussed in the sources, and Mapai later accommodated capitalism.

unions-good.rationale: The Histadrut was the central institution of the movement and Ben-Gurion helped found it as the engine of building a Jewish economy; unions were also an employer and state-builder.

property-fundamental.rationale: Land was held nationally through the Jewish National Fund and cooperative settlements, and labor-based claims outweighed ownership claims, but Labor Zionism never opposed all private property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: A labor-led economy with strong collective institutions implies support for regulation; not directly documented.

cut-welfare.rationale: A socialist-oriented movement that built its own social institutions would oppose cutting welfare, an inference from its principles.

worker-ownership.rationale: Kibbutzim and Histadrut-owned firms embodied collective worker ownership, but this was one model among several and not required of every business.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Sources do not address surveillance; adherents are split between civil-liberty and security-minded instincts.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No source addresses drugs; Labor Zionist tradition was puritanical about work but liberal parties later split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents have no settled doctrine on speech restriction.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement was party-and-union based and democratic, though Ben-Gurion was a dominant leader and favoured state authority over sectarian bodies.

state-harmful.rationale: Labor Zionists set out to build a state and Ben-Gurion's statism put loyalty to the state first, so the claim that the state is harmful is rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; the movement valued armed self-defence through the Haganah but under national institutions' control.

empower-police-military.rationale: Ben-Gurion founded the IDF, dissolved rival militias and favoured military deterrence; Mapai prized Jewish self-defence under national control.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the movement's moral earnestness about labor and pioneering; nothing documented.

decide-locally.rationale: Ben-Gurion's mamlachtiut subordinated local and party bodies to a central state and pushed a single state school system.

rehabilitation.rationale: Socialist humanism implies a rehabilitative approach, but penal policy is not documented in the sources.

traditional-family.rationale: The secular kibbutz experimented with collective child-rearing while the wider movement allied with religious parties; adherents are split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic for the founding strand; modern Labor-aligned Israelis lean in favour but historic mainstream was silent, so treated as split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed in the sources; Mapai-era politics compromised with religious partners.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement was secular and made labor its moral code, yet Mapai allied with religious Mizrachi parties and accepted a role for religion in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; the framework concerns Jewish national and class emancipation rather than racial redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; kibbutz ideals of equal labor are suggestive but not a doctrine on gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Reviving Hebrew and building an authentic Jewish national culture rooted in the land was central; Ben-Gurion saw Hebrew as central to Zionism.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement was a revolutionary settlement project that built new institutions, though Mapai's socialism was gradual and pragmatic.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Mass Jewish immigration was Israel's top priority for Ben-Gurion and the heart of the Zionist project, so reducing it is rejected; this is read as general immigration policy for Jews.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Labor Zionists relied on the UN partition decision yet put national self-reliance first; not clearly documented.

free-trade.rationale: A state-led labor economy built on self-sufficiency suggests scepticism of free trade, inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Ben-Gurion emphasised Jewish self-reliance and state loyalty, though the movement also belonged to the Socialist International; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; no clear doctrine either way.

open-borders.rationale: The movement wanted a Jewish state with a Jewish majority and controlled immigration, which conflicts with open borders for all; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Gordon's nature philosophy was critical of exploitation, but the movement as a whole prized economic development and absorbing immigrants.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic for the founding strand; modern Labor leans in favour but not documented.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Labor Zionists prized development, irrigation and industry to absorb immigrants, but did not hold a technological-salvation creed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, although Ben-Gurion pursued nuclear capacity for security; treated as split on energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Borochov spoke of revolutionary proletariat but Mapai rejected all-out revolt against the Mandate and pursued pragmatic gradualism.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between democratic and technocratic state-building.

central-planning.rationale: Labor Zionists favoured a planned labor-sector economy but accepted a mixed economy; planning was never total.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cooperative and Histadrut firms operating in a market setting resemble this view, though not stated in those terms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land was nationalised through the Jewish National Fund rather than taxed, so a land-value tax is not its programme; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Egalitarian socialist leaning suggests support; not documented.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement valued work as a moral value, which cuts against unconditional income, but welfare support pulls the other way.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Building a Jewish industrial base and self-sufficiency suggests protection, inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Mapai and the Histadrut directed development through Jewish institutions and Ben-Gurion wanted a Jewish economy built under national leadership.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Smallholder moshavim were a Labor Zionist form, but collective settlement and union enterprises were equally central.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Labor Zionism built a wage-and-union economy; Borochov sought a normal working-class base for struggle, not the abolition of wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A state-building socialist movement would reject abolishing central banks; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Histadrut combined union and employer roles and Mapai ran statist tripartite bargaining, but state-set wages are not an explicit principle.

one-party-rule.rationale: Mapai led through elections and coalitions with a multiparty system, though it dominated; it banned factions inside itself, not rival parties.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: A secular socialist and republican movement; no source suggests support for hereditary monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Mapai won repeated elections and governed parliamentarily; Labor Zionists fought the Revisionists politically and built democratic institutions.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; Israeli Labor practice was party-list parliamentary politics.

workers-councils.rationale: The movement valued workers' institutions such as the Histadrut but ran a parliamentary state, so councils replacing parliaments is not its programme.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from commitment to national self-determination and a unitary state; not addressed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Egalitarian socialist outlook rejects innate fitness to rule; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Labor Zionism opposed terrorism and reprisals on individuals yet accepted organised armed self-defence and resistance to the British.

war-builds-character.rationale: Gordon was pacifist and Ben-Gurion favoured defence, so glorifying war conflicts with the movement's labor ethos; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement was secular but Mapai allied with religious parties and accepted a religious role in some state matters.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Labor Zionists were mostly secular and founded a secular-national state; Gordon's religion of labor was a non-halakhic mysticism.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Ben-Gurion dissolved rival militias and made defense a state monopoly under the IDF.

military-superiority.rationale: Ben-Gurion founded the IDF and favoured military deterrence as core to Israel's survival.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Labor Zionism's aim was a Jewish state with a Jewish majority built by Jewish labor, though Arab citizens were accepted as a minority.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Borochov was Marxist on class struggle but Gordon rejected it and Mapai held 'from class to nation'; the movement is split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Kibbutz egalitarianism is notable but mainstream Mapai socialism was pragmatic; split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The movement's own settlement claim held that Jews should build their national home in the land; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; Israel took German reparations itself, but colonial reparations are a separate issue.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement was nationalist and state-centred; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Labor Zionism treated labor and the collective national project as the moral core, opposing selfish individualism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Gordon and pioneers stressed duty to labor and the nation, and Ben-Gurion stressed loyalty to the state, though rights were also honoured.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Gordon held cosmos, nature and humanity are an organic unity and criticised treating nature as a commodity.

limit-population.rationale: A movement that wanted mass immigration and a larger Jewish population would oppose limiting growth; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Gordon criticised alienation from nature but the movement as a whole built industry and the Histadrut economy.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed, and valuing institutions suggests caution about disruption.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement was forward-looking and revolutionary in remaking Jewish society, aiming at a new self-reliant Jew.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Mapai's socialism was pragmatic rather than doctrinaire, and Ben-Gurion repeatedly put practical state-building over theory.

direct-action.rationale: Labor Zionism worked through institutions and elections though it used settlement and defiance of British restrictions; mixed.

means-match-ends.rationale: The kibbutz and Gordon's labor ethic held that building the new society required living by its values, an interpretation not stated directly.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Labor Zionism wanted settled agriculture, industry and a state, not a hunter-gatherer life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Gordon prized manual labor and the kibbutz rotated tasks, but the movement built an industrial economy; division of labor was not abolished.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Kibbutz practice approached 'to each according to need' while the broader movement used wages; split.

production-for-use.rationale: The movement favoured production serving national and workers' needs through cooperatives, but also accepted market activity.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Borochov's Marxism held this but Gordon and Mapai's pragmatic socialism did not; the movement is split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Mapai's socialism was pragmatic and democratic, not Marxist, and rejected dictatorial rule.

collective-farming.rationale: The kibbutz was the emblem of Labor Zionism, but moshavim and individual farms existed too, so support is moderate.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Borochov analysed capitalism's international conflict but Mapai did not adopt this thesis; split.

taxation-theft.rationale: A collectivist, state-building movement rejects this libertarian claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no doctrine either way.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement defined Jews as a national group with collective rights to a homeland and gave weight to collective institutions.

conscription.rationale: The IDF under Ben-Gurion was a conscript army, and Jewish self-defense under national institutions was core.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Labor Zionism argued Jews needed a homeland to end exile and built democratic institutions; exit as the main check runs against it.

state-as-business.rationale: A statist, socialist movement rejects running government like a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: Socialist commitment to giving workers material means for emancipation suggests agreement, inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: None of the sources discuss media or university power, and adherents have no shared doctrine on it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Labor Zionism defined Jews as a nation shaped by material conditions (Borochov) rather than racial hierarchy; inferred rejection.

organic-representation.rationale: Mapai worked through parties and the Histadrut federation, yet this is closer to unions than to organic representation; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Mapai was a pragmatic democratic party; mamlachtiut meant state primacy in public institutions, not totalitarian control.

national-rebirth.rationale: Labor Zionism aimed at the regeneration of the Jewish people through return to the land and labor, though 'decadence' is not its framing.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The mainstream accepted partition in 1937 and 1947 and later pursued land for peace; only a Greater Israel minority sought expansion after 1967.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A modern democratic movement; no source suggests personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Labor Zionism glorified free self-labor on the land and opposed exploitative arrangements.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Labor Zionist texts here take no stance on the politics of knowledge, so the answer is neutral by absence.

universal-morality.rationale: Gordon's organic mystical humanism partly suggests it, but the movement was not committed to a doctrine; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Mapai's 'from class to people' suggested a national common good, yet interests were bargained through parties and unions.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The founding goal of Labor Zionism: a Jewish national home built by Jewish workers; Ben-Gurion declared the state in 1948.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Ben-Gurion made ingathering of exiles and aliyah Israel's top priority, and the movement founded itself on Jewish immigration.

revive-national-language.rationale: Reviving Hebrew was part of Zionism, and Ben-Gurion saw Hebrew as central to authentic Zionism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The kibbutz and Histadrut-owned enterprises had worker participation, though not in all companies.

school-vouchers.rationale: Ben-Gurion pushed a single state education system to replace party-run schools, the opposite of voucher choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: A socialist-oriented, development-minded movement leans toward state spending; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: The movement sought a labor-led economy, so tying political freedom to economic freedom is not its view; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Pioneer example (halutzim) was valued but the movement built laws and institutions.

national-self-determination.rationale: Borochov grounded national claims on territory for oppressed nations and Zionism claims self-determination for Jews.

force-without-un.rationale: Ben-Gurion put Israeli security above external approval, though early Mapai relied on the UN partition plan.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The movement was secular but Gordon was a mystic and Mapai allied with religious parties; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; Histadrut benefits were tied to membership and the movement was ambivalent about Arab inclusion.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The ethic of labor as a moral value, especially Gordon's, suggests agreement, inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Mapai's 'from class to nation' favoured national over class interests while the Histadrut was a labor body; split with Borochovist class-struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement wanted to renew Jewish culture while rooting it in Hebrew and Jewish tradition, not sacrifice institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Labor Zionism allied with Western powers and the Socialist International, not a front against them; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: 'From class to nation' made workers the national force; Labor Zionism organised Jewish workers as a nation rather than internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The kibbutz ideal asserted equal labor for women although practice was uneven; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: A modern socialist movement that built banks and credit institutions would not ban interest; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Labor Zionism sought a Jewish state and accepted Arab citizens, not racial segregation law.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Borochov's Marxism implies it while Mapai's statism treated the state as national; split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is not addressed by the founding strand, and adherents are not united on it today.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The ingathering of exiles aimed at a Hebrew-speaking national culture, expecting immigrants to join it (the 'melting pot').

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in the movement's doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Israel adopted national list PR with Mapai's governing role; Labor Zionists did not oppose it, though not documented.

national-mission.rationale: Ben-Gurion spoke of Israel as a light to the nations, but spreading its government to others is not a program; split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources do not address structural patriarchy; kibbutz equality ideals are suggestive but not a doctrine.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Labor Zionists were the governing elite until 1977, and would reject the characterization; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not a Labor Zionist position; inferred from humanist socialism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; Mapai opposed reprisals on individual Arabs yet Ben-Gurion backed retaliatory raids; split.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A labor-led movement that built an extensive Histadrut sector and state institutions opposes a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed; Zionism opposed assimilation of Jews but this is a different matter; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Socialist humanist values, though practice toward Arabs was contested; mainstream endorsed formal equality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Mapai's pragmatic socialism did not require world revolution; Borochov was internationalist but held local proletarianization first.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Adherents regard Zionism as a national return, not colonialism, a position that critics dispute.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Mapai maintained religious jurisdiction over personal status as part of its alliance with religious parties.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; secular movement but accommodation to religious parties; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a Labor Zionist concern; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Mapai's state education system coexisted with religious schools and its religious allies; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mapai governed through elections and parliamentary coalitions.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance policy is not discussed in the sources, so no stated position can be drawn.

population-transfer.rationale: Historians dispute whether Ben-Gurion supported expulsion; the mainstream did not adopt it as doctrine, though Mapai favoured keeping refugees out.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Gordon was pacifist, but Ben-Gurion and Mapai accepted retaliatory force and war, so the absolute claim is rejected by the mainstream.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not documented; Ben-Gurion banned militias, but outlawing parties is not addressed.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory does not appear in the sources, so no position is inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Parliamentary democracy with courts; Mapai accepted it, but the point is inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Borochov's Poale Zion was a party of the working class, yet Mapai was a mass party rather than a Leninist vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Socialist orientation suggests support, though not documented.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is not addressed in the sources; cooperative housing and ownership both appear in the movement's history.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Histadrut, the main labor union, was central to the movement and would resist such restrictions.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not addressed; the melting pot ideal concerned Jewish communities.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not a Labor Zionist idea; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Israel kept Mandatory emergency regulations while Mapai governed, but sources do not give the movement's own doctrine.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State direction of the economy suggests support, though not documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: Mapai ran a multiparty democracy; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Ben-Gurion dissolved party militias such as the Palmach and made the IDF a state army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The movement favoured quick citizenship for Jewish immigrants; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for representatives is not addressed, though Histadrut egalitarian ideals could point either way.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Mapai's 1942 convention banned factions inside the party, showing a binding-discipline tradition.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Israel adopted a parliamentary cabinet under Mapai leadership; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement was secular and nationalist and rejected rule by clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Mapai backed Jewish units fighting alongside Britain against the Nazis, an opposite of revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from socialist liberal culture.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits for presidents are not addressed; Israel's presidency is parliamentary and ceremonial.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall votes are not discussed; Israeli Labor politics used party-list elections without recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Mapai sought allies and the Socialist International; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Collective and union housing existed, but abolishing rental is not a program.

people-in-arms.rationale: Haganah and kibbutz citizen-defense had militia aspects but Ben-Gurion built a professional state army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Gordon's religion of labor and kibbutz ideology idealized agricultural life as regenerative over exile city life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The question of reunifying a divided nation does not arise in the sources, so no stand is inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The sources do not address cultural hierarchy, and a movement stressing Jewish national revival gives no clear answer.

death-penalty.rationale: Israel abolished the death penalty for ordinary crimes in 1954 under Mapai; the only exceptions were Nazi crimes, treason and such, and the movement's own doctrine is not documented.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred secular progressive leaning; not documented.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography law is not addressed in the sources, and adherents have no doctrine on it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Law of Return rested on Jewish descent; read by analogy, adherents accept descent-based claims.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; Arab citizens were accepted but Hebrew was the national language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Mapai exempted yeshiva students and allowed religious accommodations in its alliance, but the doctrine is not documented.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style individuality is not discussed; the pioneering ethic prized collective conformity but not dogmatically.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt cancellation for poor countries is not addressed in the sources, so no position is drawn.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Borochov and Labor Zionists held that national independence needed a restructured Jewish economy built by workers.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Israel never adopted a written constitution under Mapai; the movement had no stated view.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Mapai ran a democracy while pursuing development; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; Labor Israel later ran aid programs but the doctrine is not documented.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Ben-Gurion pursued Israel's own deterrent, though the sources do not describe it.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Israel's president is elected by the Knesset, with Mapai leading; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A state-led economy implies government control of money policy; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Mainstream Labor Zionists backed giving up territory; by Oslo it was Labor's central policy, though a minority formed the Greater Israel movement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Land was held nationally and labor-based claims came before ownership, consistent with property serving the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Labor Zionist sources here do not characterise the Soviet Union, and adherents were divided in their attitudes to it.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Mapai's socialism was not Marxist-Leninist, so the withering-away debate did not apply, though security fears favoured a strong state.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement stressed labor and cooperation rather than struggle between peoples as the engine of progress; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Manual labor and working the land are morally regenerating and should be honored above other occupations.
missingStatements.rationale: Gordon's religion of labor and the kibbutz ideal made working the soil the route to personal and national renewal.
missingStatements.declined: Cultural-ethical valuation of manual labor specific to this movement; rural-life-healthier does not capture it and a new statement is not worth the bank cost.

missingStatements.text: A people living in exile should return to a homeland of its own and become workers there rather than remain a nation of middlemen.
missingStatements.rationale: Borochov's inverted pyramid and Gordon's call to labor held that normalizing the Jewish occupational structure required a territorial base.

missingStatements.text: Trade unions should own and run enterprises as well as bargain over wages.
missingStatements.rationale: The Histadrut combined union, employer and settlement functions, building a labor-owned economic sector.

notes: Strands diverge: Borochov's Marxist class struggle, Gordon's non-Marxist nationalism and Mapai's pragmatic statism. After 1967 a minority sought Greater Israel while most backed territorial compromise; the profile follows the mainstream.
